Pharaoh Frog Hopán — Tile long-hop review
Design Document
Version 1.0 | October 19, 2026
Scoped design review. Resource gating remains exploratory; current game rules are unchanged.
Authorship and approval are independent. AI proposals retain their origin after approval. Documented design
does not prove implementation or testing.

Recommendation and scope
AI recommendation, pending your decision: keep the existing Tile Hop rules while testing a separate charged-
hop variant. If you want long hop to be a resource, prefer one banked charge that recharges after 10 successful
ordinary hops over mandatory fragments. Ten is a provisional test value, not a measured optimum; do not
begin at 25. A resource restriction adds planning, but is not inherently a novice assist.
The goal inferred from your question is to make the moment of spending a long hop deliberate and
understandable while retaining novice agency. This review examines the current code and authored routes at
source 491ad955ed19a030148bbed090e15600abd6907d. It makes no gameplay, level, publication or
progression changes. The public site remains v22.

What the current game demonstrates
Current implementation: cardinal one- and two-cell hops both take 0.34 simulation seconds, with brief input
recovery. Long hop can clear intermediate water, scenery, enemies and projectiles; walls and cheese walls still
block it. Takeoff and landing remain vulnerable. There is no power-charge economy. The new readiness
indicator describes the existing action gate, not a new cooldown.
Fresh hazard-active controller runs completed Big Hop Boulevard in 61 hops with 11 long hops, and Your Move
Crossing in 70 hops with eight long hops. Boulevard uses three consecutive long hops at actions 37–39;
Crossing uses long hops at actions 44 and 46. Alternate traffic timing and the Crossing shortcut also complete.
These are automated successful routes, not novice playtests or proof that no alternative routes exist.
A strict recharge of 10–25 ordinary hops would invalidate these successful sequences without backtracking,
refills or layout changes. Some crossings clear water, so missing a charge can become a progression problem
rather than simply a slower route. In Move with me, each accepted hop also advances hazards; recharge by
movement therefore changes encounter timing.

Compare the options
 Rule                  Likely benefit                          Main cost

 Current unlimited     Reliable traversal; learn               May allow repetitive long hopping; dominance is
 hop                   takeoff/landing timing                  not yet established

 Pickup-only charge    Author controls where power is          Missed/spent pickups can strand novices;
 or fragments          available; exploration reward           fragments add collection and HUD burden

 Banked movement       Availability is predictable; player     Can encourage safe back-and-forth grinding and
 recharge              chooses when to spend                   hoarding; requires compatible levels


Channel Hideo | 1

Provisional experiment: one stored charge
AI proposal A-01: start a test level with one charge. A successful long hop spends it; an attempted blocked hop
spends nothing. Recharge after 10 successfully completed ordinary hops, including backtracking. Do not count
blocked inputs, time spent idle, menu use or distance carried by a log. Once full, hold the charge until the
player uses it; no expiry and no multi-charge stockpile. Display Ready or a remaining-hop counter in the same
control.
Restore a full charge when retrying at a checkpoint, and guarantee that every mandatory crossing is reachable
with the resource rules. For a one-charge design, Boulevard’s consecutive water-hop section needs refills at
safe landings or a different layout. A pickup can optionally refill the same charge, but do not introduce
fragments in the first test. These are proposals, not adopted requirements.
Example: the player spends a charge crossing one danger lane, then has eight normal hops remaining after
moving two steps. They may save the next full charge for a turret or detour. Counterexample: a novice uses it
one tile before mandatory water; if there is no safe refill or traversable recharge space, the design has failed
regardless of the cooldown number.
Allow simple back-and-forth recharge in the prototype rather than hiding a unique-tile rule. It matches your
tolerance for an abusable but understandable system. Measure whether players choose repetitive farming; if
they do, adjust encounter/refill placement or abandon the charge rule instead of treating the symptom as
cheating.

Decision, validation and limits
Recommended order: first decide whether long hop is the mode’s everyday traversal verb or a deliberately
scarce tactical tool. If the latter, approve a small optional prototype before changing existing tours. Compare
unlimited baseline against one stored charge / 10 ordinary hops on an authored test map. Test 25 only if 10
still removes meaningful choices and the longer recharge does not create repeated dead time.
Observe a small qualitative pilot with novices, intermediate players and an experienced route optimizer, on
keyboard and touch. Ask players to predict when the next long hop is available; record intentional attempts
while empty, deaths caused by resource misunderstanding, recharge-only backtracking, charge hoarding and
whether short-hop alternatives feel worthwhile. Do not infer enjoyment from route completion alone.
Stop or revise if any required gate can strand a valid playthrough, checkpoint retry reproduces a resource trap,
or players repeatedly believe the input failed. Acceptance evidence should include safe recovery from
spending early and a clear tactical choice beyond merely waiting or grinding. No human pilot or restricted-
charge simulation was run in this review.
Coverage: movement, resource incentives, level dependencies, checkpoint recovery and readiness feedback
reviewed. Whole-game economy, visual redesign, audio and additional unlocks are intentionally outside scope.
No implementation or deployment decision is recorded.

Sources and revision
Primary evidence: repository game/scripts/tile_rules.gd; main.gd checkpoint retry and readiness UI;
game/tests/tile_demo_routes.gd; docs/TILE_LEVEL_REDESIGN.md. Temporary route instrumentation ran the
actual controller with active hazards at fixed 1/60 simulation steps, then was removed. Four successful routes
and long-hop indices are retained in route-evidence.json. Accelerated test time is not a device-performance
measurement.
Review version 1.0, October 19, 2026. Human request: consider a powerup, power fragments, or a 10–25-tile
cooldown, accepting possible abuse if novices gain perceived control/fairness. Analysis and provisional rules
are AI-origin synthesis using Channel Hideo and Balancewright. No external developer endorsement or
measured novice preference is claimed.
Channel Hideo | 2

Human contributions
H-01 Consider resource-gated long hop
Origin HUMAN | Status exploratory | Implementation not started
Powerup, power fragments, or a 10–25-tile cooldown; possible abuse may be acceptable if novices feel more
control and fairness.
Source User message of October 19, 2026
Priority Not ranked; assistant recommendation: Investigate now. Preserve player agency and avoid resource
softlocks while testing the intended tactical choice.

AI proposals and contributions
A-01 Prototype one banked charge / 10 ordinary hops
Origin AI | Status proposed | Implementation not started
One charge, clear countdown, blocked inputs free, checkpoint refill and mandatory-crossing safety; fragments
deferred for the first experiment.
Source This review of current Hopán source and route instrumentation
Priority Not ranked; assistant recommendation: First prototype if approved. Preserve player agency and avoid
resource softlocks while testing the intended tactical choice.

A-02 Preserve current tours until the rule is tested
Origin AI | Status proposed | Implementation not started
Keep baseline rules available; current successful routes contain tightly grouped long hops and require redesign
or guaranteed refills before restriction.
Source This review of current Hopán source and route instrumentation
Priority Not ranked; assistant recommendation: Recommended now. Preserve player agency and avoid
resource softlocks while testing the intended tactical choice.

Approved decision index
No approved decisions are recorded. Proposals remain provisional.
